images.title: Each new shape has half the area
images.purpose: Show a nested diamond pattern in which each shape, made by joining midpoints, has half the area of the one around it.
images.composition: Four nested shapes centred on white, alternating diamond and square, each labelled with its area.
images.exact_structure: One large square standing on a corner (a diamond) of area 64, about 80 percent of the frame height, centred, outline and fill pale teal #0072B2. Joining the midpoints of its 4 sides gives an upright square of area 32, filled amber #E69F00. Joining the midpoints of that square gives a diamond of area 16, filled teal #0072B2. Joining the midpoints of that gives an upright square of area 8, filled amber #E69F00. Exactly 4 shapes, all centred on the same point, thin dark outlines. Each area number sits in a column to the right of the pattern, joined by a short thin leader line to a point on its own shape's outline, top to bottom: '64', '32', '16', '8'. Under that column, 'half each time'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Joining the midpoints keeps exactly half the area each time.

image_decisions.why: The halving is the mathematics inside the blanket pattern; nested shapes make it countable.
